about: Chapter 3, Angles as Turns: 65 patterns, three or four for each of the 15 skills (1 and 2 marks), three 3-mark and three 5-mark long answers in steps (#208), and three 4-mark case studies, drawn from the chapter's 500 questions. Directions are North, East, South and West only and turns are fractions of a full turn (the chapter uses no degrees). All DRAFT until Ashalatha approves them.

patterns.text: {ob.o} turns {r.f} of a complete turn. What is this turn called?

wrong.mistake: names a different part of a turn: confuses quarter, half and three-quarter turns
names a different part of a turn: confuses quarter, half and three-quarter turns
names a different part of a turn: confuses quarter, half and three-quarter turns

patterns.hint: Match the fraction with equal parts of one whole turn: 1/4 is one of four equal parts.
patterns.explanation: {r.f} of a complete turn is called: {r.c}.
patterns.notes: The fraction is 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 or 4/4; the four turn names are always the options. Eight pointer contexts.
patterns.misconception: Treats the distance travelled by a point as the size of the turn, or confuses half and quarter turns.

patterns.text: {ob.o} has turned {a}/{n} of a full turn. What fraction of a turn is still needed to complete the full turn?
patterns.hint: A full turn is {n}/{n}. Take away the part already turned.
patterns.explanation: A full turn is {n}/{n}. {n}/{n} − {a}/{n} = {n - a}/{n}, so {n - a}/{n} of a turn is still needed.
patterns.notes: Denominator 5 to 12; the part turned and the part left are both already in simplest form, so there is one way to write the answer.
patterns.misconception: Treats the distance travelled by a point as the size of the turn, or confuses half and quarter turns.

patterns.text: A full turn of {ob.t} is divided into {m.n} equal mini-turns. How many mini-turns make {m.w}?
patterns.hint: A quarter turn is 1 of 4 equal parts of the full turn. How many mini-turns is that?
patterns.explanation: {m.n} mini-turns make a full turn, so a quarter turn is {m.n} ÷ 4 = {m.n // 4} mini-turns, and {m.w} is {m.ans} mini-turns.
patterns.notes: A full turn split into 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 or 24 mini-turns; asks for a quarter, half or three-quarter turn.
patterns.misconception: Treats the distance travelled by a point as the size of the turn, or confuses half and quarter turns.

steps.text: Adds the quarter turns: {t.a} + {t.b} = {t.k} quarter turns.

patterns.hint: Count all the quarter turns. Four quarter turns make a full turn.
patterns.explanation: {t.a} + {t.b} = {t.k} quarter turns. Four quarter turns make a full turn, so {t.k} quarter turns is: {t.c}.
patterns.notes: 1 to 4 quarter turns, then 1 to 4 more (total 3 to 6 quarter turns). The two numbers differ and multiply to at most 8, so multiplying or taking one from the other gives a wrong option; the right answer is the second or third largest option.
patterns.misconception: Treats the distance travelled by a point as the size of the turn, or confuses half and quarter turns.

patterns.text: {who.name} draws a design with {a} squares, {b} rectangles and {c} triangles. None of the triangles has a right angle. How many right-angle corners are there in the design altogether?

steps.text: Counts 4 right angles in each square and rectangle and none in the triangles.

patterns.hint: Every square and every rectangle has 4 right-angle corners. Do the triangles add any?
patterns.explanation: Squares and rectangles each have 4 right angles: 4 × ({a} + {b}) = {4 * (a + b)}. The triangles have no right angles, so there are {4 * (a + b)} right-angle corners.
patterns.notes: 2 to 9 squares, 2 to 8 rectangles and 2 to 6 triangles with no right angle (so counting every corner gives a wrong answer).
patterns.misconception: Assumes every visible corner is a right angle without comparing it with a quarter turn.

patterns.notes: Units of 1/4 to 1/24 turn (even denominators); 1 to 4 straight angles.
patterns.misconception: Confuses a straight angle with a full turn because both may appear to return to a line.

patterns.misconception: Confuses a straight angle with a full turn because both may appear to return to a line.

patterns.text: {ob.o} moves {kk.w} round a circle divided into 8 equal spaces. Write the turn as a fraction of a full turn, in simplest form.

patterns.notes: 1 to 7 spaces of an eighth-turn circle; answer in simplest form (2/8 is written 1/4).

patterns.explanation: {x.f} = {x.c}: both the numerator and the denominator are multiplied by {x.k}.
patterns.notes: 11 starting fractions (halves to eighths); multiplied by 2, 3 or 4.
patterns.misconception: Adds the same number to numerator and denominator rather than scaling both.

patterns.text: Complete the equivalent turn: {ab.a}/{ab.b} = {ab.a * k}/□. What number goes in the box?
patterns.hint: What was the numerator multiplied by? Do the same to the denominator.
patterns.explanation: {ab.a} × {k} = {ab.a * k}, so the denominator is {ab.b} × {k} = {ab.b * k}: {ab.a}/{ab.b} = {ab.a * k}/{ab.b * k}.
patterns.notes: 11 starting fractions; multiplied by 2 to 6.
patterns.misconception: Adds the same number to numerator and denominator rather than scaling both.

patterns.text: Complete the equivalent turn: {ab.a}/{ab.b} = □/{ab.b * k}. What number goes in the box?
patterns.hint: How many times larger is the new denominator? Make the numerator that many times larger too.
patterns.explanation: {ab.b * k} ÷ {ab.b} = {k}, so the numerator is {ab.a} × {k} = {ab.a * k}: {ab.a}/{ab.b} = {ab.a * k}/{ab.b * k}.

patterns.text: {ctx} has {x.n} equal spaces. How many spaces make a turn equivalent to {x.f} of a full turn?

patterns.text: {ob.o} turns {a}/{n} of a full turn and then {b}/{n} in the same direction. Give the total turn in simplest form.
patterns.hint: Add the numerators. The denominator stays {n}, because the parts are the same size. Then simplify.
patterns.explanation: {a}/{n} + {b}/{n} = {a + b}/{n} = {frac(a + b, n):fraction} of a full turn.
patterns.notes: Same denominator 6, 8, 10, 12 or 16; the total is less than a full turn.
patterns.misconception: Adds denominators when combining equal fractional-turn units.

patterns.text: A total turn of {t}/{n} is made of two parts. One part is {a}/{n}. What is the other part? Give it in simplest form.

patterns.explanation: {t}/{n} − {a}/{n} = {t - a}/{n} = {frac(t - a, n):fraction}.
patterns.notes: Same denominator 6 to 16; total 3/n to (n−1)/n.
patterns.misconception: Adds denominators when combining equal fractional-turn units.

patterns.text: {x.ctx} opens 1/{x.p} turn, then a further 1/{x.q} turn in the same direction. What is the total turn, in simplest form?

patterns.explanation: 1/{x.p} = {x.l // x.p}/{x.l} and 1/{x.q} = {x.l // x.q}/{x.l}. Together: {x.l // x.p + x.l // x.q}/{x.l} = {x.t} of a full turn.
patterns.notes: Two unit-fraction turns from one family (halves, quarters, eighths; thirds, sixths, twelfths; fifths and tenths), in either order. A book cover never opens more than a half turn.

patterns.notes: Any two clock numbers at least two spaces apart clockwise (it may pass 12).
patterns.misconception: Uses the number written on the clock as the number of minutes moved.

parts.text: (d) How many more spaces must the fan open to make a straight angle?
parts.hint: A straight angle is half the circle: {x.n} ÷ 2 spaces.
